claim: HSV-1 H129-G4 injected in the femur marrow labels GFP+ neurons in the ARC area at 5 days post infection.
source: an anterograde multisynaptic tracer herpes simplex virus type 1 (HSV-1) H129-G4 was directly injected in the femur marrow in 3-month-old wild-type mice (Zeng et al., 2017), GFP labeled neurons in ARC area has been detected at 5 days post infection (dpi) (Figure 1A).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data from viral tracing experiments shown in Figure 1A and described in the text, with citation to Zeng et al., 2017 for the tracer method.

claim: Serum NPY concentration is significantly elevated in 3-month-old AvilCre:Ntrk1fl/fl mice compared with WT littermates.
source: Serum NPY concentration was significantly elevated in 3-month-old AvilCre:Ntrk1fl/fl mice compared with that of WT littermates (Figure 1B).
evidence: The claim is supported by ELISA data shown in Figure 1B comparing serum NPY levels between genotypes.

claim: NPY expression is significantly increased in the ARC of AvilCre:Ntrk1fl/fl mice.
source: Immunostaining of the hypothalamus showed that NPY expression was also significantly increased in the ARC of AvilCre:Ntrk1fl/fl mice (Figure 1C).
evidence: The claim is supported by immunofluorescence staining data shown in Figure 1C.

claim: Food intake increased in AvilCre:Ntrk1fl/fl mice compared with WT littermates.
source: Moreover, food intake increased in AvilCre:Ntrk1fl/fl mice compared with WT littermates (Figure 1D).
evidence: The claim is supported by quantitative food intake measurements shown in Figure 1D.

claim: Total body weight remained unchanged in AvilCre:Ntrk1fl/fl mice compared to WT littermates.
source: Whereas total body weight remained unchanged (Figure 1E)
evidence: The claim is supported by body weight measurements shown in Figure 1E.

claim: The size and weight of gonadal and inguinal fat pads increased significantly in AvilCre:Ntrk1fl/fl mice compared with WT mice.
source: the size and weight of gonadal and inguinal fat pads increased significantly in AvilCre:Ntrk1fl/fl mice compared with WT mice (Figure 1F).
evidence: The claim is supported by quantitative measurements of fat pad weights shown in Figure 1F.

claim: qNMR detected a significant increase in the fat mass of adult (3-month-old) but not young (1-month-old) AvilCre:Ntrk1fl/fl mice.
source: Accordingly, echo magnetic resonance imaging (qNMR) detected a significant increase in the fat mass of adult (3-month-old) but not young (1-month-old) AvilCre:Ntrk1fl/fl mice (Figure 1G).
evidence: The claim is supported by qNMR measurements of fat mass shown in Figure 1G.

claim: No significant differences in lean mass were found in the 1- or 3-month-old groups between WT and AvilCre:Ntrk1fl/fl mice.
source: Interestingly, no significant differences in lean mass were found in the 1- or 3-month-old groups (Figure 1H).
evidence: The claim is supported by qNMR measurements of lean mass shown in Figure 1H.

claim: NPY levels in serum increased significantly 5 and 7 days after DTX injection in AvilCre:Rosa26lsl-DTR mice.
source: Indeed, NPY levels in serum increased significantly 5 and 7 days after DTX injection (Figure 1I)
evidence: The claim is supported by ELISA measurements of serum NPY shown in Figure 1I.

claim: NPY expression in the ARC increased significantly 7 days after DTX injection in AvilCre:Rosa26lsl-DTR mice.
source: and NPY expression in the ARC increased significantly 7 days after DTX injection, as shown by immunostaining of hypothalamus sections (Figure 1J).
evidence: The claim is supported by immunofluorescence staining data shown in Figure 1J.

claim: Daily food intake increased significantly in the DTX group of AvilCre:Rosa26lsl-DTR mice.
source: Daily food intake also increased significantly in the DTX group (Figure 1K).
evidence: The claim is supported by food intake measurements shown in Figure 1K.

claim: Gonadal and inguinal fat pad size and weight increased significantly in DTX-treated AvilCre:Rosa26lsl-DTR mice.
source: Consistent with results in AvilCre:Ntrk1fl/fl mice, gonadal and inguinal fat pad size and weight increased significantly (Figure 1L)
evidence: The claim is supported by fat pad weight measurements shown in Figure 1L.

claim: qNMR validated much higher fat mass in the DTX group of AvilCre:Rosa26lsl-DTR mice.
source: and qNMR validated much higher fat mass in the DTX group (Figure 1M)
evidence: The claim is supported by qNMR measurements shown in Figure 1M.

claim: No significant difference in lean mass was found between the DTX and vehicle groups of AvilCre:Rosa26lsl-DTR mice.
source: whereas no significant difference in lean mass was found between the DTX and vehicle groups (Figure 1N).
evidence: The claim is supported by qNMR measurements shown in Figure 1N.

claim: Peripheral sensory nerves regulate NPY expression in the hypothalamus ARC for metabolism of adipose tissue.
source: Our results show that peripheral sensory nerves regulate NPY expression in the hypothalamus ARC for metabolism of adipose tissue.
evidence: The claim is an interpretation of the experimental data from sensory denervation experiments showing changes in NPY expression and fat metabolism.

claim: SW033291 elevated PGE2 concentration in bone marrow but not in the hypothalamus.
source: The SW033291 group had a significantly higher PGE2 concentration in bone marrow compared with the vehicle group (Figure 2A, left), but no difference in PGE2 concentration was found between groups when analyzing the hypothalamic interstitium (Figure 2A, right).
evidence: The claim is supported by ELISA measurements of PGE2 in bone marrow and hypothalamus shown in Figure 2A.

claim: WT mice treated with SW033291 had significantly lower Npy gene expression in the ARC and significantly lower serum NPY level compared with the vehicle group.
source: Compared with the vehicle group, WT mice treated with SW033291 had significantly lower Npy gene expression in the ARC and significantly lower serum NPY level (Figure 2B and C).
evidence: The claim is supported by RT-PCR and ELISA data shown in Figures 2B and 2C.

claim: Serum NPY concentration is significantly higher in AvilCre:Ptger4fl/fl 3-month-old mice compared with Ptger4fl/fl littermates.
source: Serum NPY concentration and its expression in the ARC area were significantly higher in AvilCre:Ptger4fl/fl 3-month-old mice compared with that of their WT littermates Ptger4fl/fl, but no significant differences were found between the altered 1-month-old mice and the WT 1-month-old mice (Figure 2D).
evidence: The claim is supported by ELISA measurements shown in Figure 2D.

claim: The effect of PGE2 on decreased NPY expression was abolished in AvilCre:Ptger4fl/fl mice.
source: The effect of PGE2 on decreased NPY expression was abolished in AvilCre:Ptger4fl/fl mice (Figure 2E and F).
evidence: The claim is supported by ELISA and immunofluorescence data shown in Figures 2E and 2F.

claim: Food intake is significantly higher in AvilCre:Ptger4fl/fl compared with WT littermates, but no significant change was found in AvilCre:Ptger4fl/fl mice after SW033291 injection.
source: Food intake significantly higher in AvilCre:Ptger4fl/fl compared with that of their WT littermates, but no significant change was found in AvilCre:Ptger4fl/fl mice after SW033291 injection (Figure 2G).
evidence: The claim is supported by food intake measurements shown in Figure 2G.

claim: No significant change in total body weight was found in male and female mice in both AvilCre:Ptger4fl/fl and their WT littermates.
source: Moreover, no significant change in total body weight was found in male and female mice in both AvilCre:Ptger4fl/fl and their WT littermates (Figure 2H).
evidence: The claim is supported by body weight measurements shown in Figure 2H.

claim: Gonadal and inguinal fat pad weights increased significantly in AvilCre:Ptger4fl/fl mice, whereas injection of SW033291 reduced major fat pad weights in WT mice but not in AvilCre:Ptger4fl/fl mice.
source: Gonadal and inguinal fat pad weights increased significantly in AvilCre:Ptger4fl/fl mice, whereas injection of SW033291 reduced major fat pad weights in WT mice but not in AvilCre:Ptger4fl/fl mice (Figure 2I).
evidence: The claim is supported by fat pad weight measurements shown in Figure 2I.

claim: Fat mass increased significantly in AvilCre:Ptger4fl/fl mice, and injection of SW033291 reduced fat mass in WT mice but not in the AvilCre:Ptger4fl/fl mice.
source: Again, qNMR showed that fat mass increased significantly in AvilCre:Ptger4fl/fl mice, and injection of SW033291 reduced fat mass in WT mice but not in the AvilCre:Ptger4fl/fl mice (Figure 2J).
evidence: The claim is supported by qNMR measurements shown in Figure 2J.

claim: No significant differences in lean mass were found between WT and AvilCre:Ptger4fl/fl mice with or without SW033291 injection.
source: Similarly, no significant differences in lean mass were found between WT and AvilCre:Ptger4fl/fl mice with or without SW033291 injection (Figure 2K).
evidence: The claim is supported by qNMR measurements shown in Figure 2K.

claim: NPY expression in the ARC is regulated by PGE2/EP4 ascending interoceptive signaling in balance bone and adipose tissue metabolism.
source: Thus, NPY expression in the ARC was regulated by PGE2/EP4 ascending interoceptive signaling in balance bone and adipose tissue metabolism.
evidence: The claim is an interpretation of the experimental data showing that EP4 deletion in sensory nerves abolishes PGE2-mediated regulation of NPY.

claim: CREB phosphorylation and SMILE protein expression increased significantly in mice injected with SW033291.
source: CREB phosphorylation and SMILE protein expression increased significantly in mice injected with SW033291 (Figure 3A).
evidence: The claim is supported by Western blot data shown in Figure 3A.

claim: SW033291 induced specific binding of pCREB/SMILE to the most distal CREB binding site of the Npy promoter.
source: ChIP assay results showed that SW033291 induced specific binding of pCREB/SMILE to the most distal CREB binding site of the Npy promoter (Figure 3C–E).
evidence: The claim is supported by ChIP-qPCR data shown in Figures 3C-E.

claim: Expression of both SMILE and CREB phosphorylation were increased significantly in the ARC of Ptger4fl/fl mice but not in AvilCre:Ptger4fl/fl mice after SW033291 injection.
source: Immunostaining of hypothalamus sections showed that expression of both SMILE and CREB phosphorylation were increased significantly in the ARC of Ptger4fl/fl mice but not in AvilCre:Ptger4fl/fl mice (Figure 3F–G).
evidence: The claim is supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figures 3F-G.

claim: PGE2/EP4 ascending skeleton interoceptive signaling induces transcriptional repressor SMILE expression in the hypothalamus, which interacts with pCREB as a heterodimer to bind to Npy promoter therefore repressing Npy gene transcription.
source: Taken together, these results indicate that PGE2/EP4 ascending skeleton interoceptive signaling induces transcriptional repressor SMILE expression in the hypothalamus, which interacts with pCREB as a heterodimer to bind to Npy promoter therefore repressing Npy gene transcription.
evidence: The claim is an interpretation of the ChIP and immunostaining data showing SMILE/pCREB binding to Npy promoter and their increased expression after SW033291 treatment.

claim: Injection of SW033291 significantly increased bone volume and trabecular bone number in WT mice but not in AvilCre:Ptger4fl/fl mice.
source: Injection of SW033291 significantly increased bone volume and trabecular bone number in WT mice but not in AvilCre:Ptger4fl/fl mice (Figure 3—figure supplement 1A–B).
evidence: The claim is supported by μCT data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1A-B.

claim: SW033291-induced bone formation and mineral composition in WT mice was abolished in AvilCre:Ptger4fl/fl mice.
source: Calcein double-labeling confirmed that SW033291-induced bone formation and mineral composition in WT mice was abolished in AvilCre:Ptger4fl/fl mice (Figure 4A and B).
evidence: The claim is supported by calcein double-labeling data shown in Figures 4A and 4B.

claim: pCREB in osteocalcin+ osteoblastic cells was significantly increased in WT mice injected with SW033291, and no such increase in pCREB in osteoblastic cells occurred in AvilCre:Ptger4fl/fl mice.
source: Co-immunostaining of trabecular bone sections showed that pCREB in osteocalcin+ osteoblastic cells was significantly increased in WT mice injected with SW033291, and No such increase in pCREB in osteoblastic cells occurred in AvilCre:Ptger4fl/fl mice (Figure 4C and D).
evidence: The claim is supported by co-immunofluorescence staining data shown in Figures 4C and 4D.

claim: cAMP production was stimulated by SW033291 in bone marrow, and the stimulation was abolished in AvilCre:Ptger4fl/fl mice.
source: Similarly, cAMP production was stimulated by SW033291 in bone marrow, and the stimulation was abolished in AvilCre:Ptger4fl/fl mice (Figure 4E).
evidence: The claim is supported by cAMP concentration measurements shown in Figure 4E.

claim: The expression of osteogenic markers Runx2, alkaline phosphatase (Alp), and Collagen type Ia (Col1a1) increased significantly in WT mice with SW033291 injection, and these effects were eliminated in AvilCre:Ptger4fl/fl mice.
source: Reverse transcription-polymerase chain reaction (RT-PCR) showed that the expression of osteogenic markers Runx2 (Figure 4F), alkaline phosphatase (Alp), and Collagen type Ia (Col1a1) (Figure 3—figure supplement 1D) increased significantly in WT mice with SW033291 injection, and these effects were eliminated in AvilCre:Ptger4fl/fl mice.
evidence: The claim is supported by RT-PCR data shown in Figure 4F and Figure 3—figure supplement 1D.

claim: The effects of SW033291 on osteogenesis and adipogenesis inhibition were significantly abrogated in AvilCre:Ptger4fl/fl mice.
source: Importantly, co-immunostaining of perilipin and osteocalcin showed that the effects of SW033291 on osteogenesis and adipogenesis inhibition were significantly abrogated in AvilCre:Ptger4fl/fl mice (Figure 4G and H).
evidence: The claim is supported by co-immunofluorescence staining data shown in Figures 4G and 4H.

claim: SW033291 injection in WT mice caused significantly increased Fatp1 and Cpt1b expression in osteoblasts, but these effects were not present in AvilCre:Ptger4fl/fl mice.
source: As expected, SW033291 injection in WT mice caused significantly increased Fatp1 and Cpt1b expression in osteoblasts, but these effects were not present in AvilCre:Ptger4fl/fl mice (Figure 4I).
evidence: The claim is supported by RT-PCR data shown in Figure 4I.

claim: NPY downregulated by PGE2/EP4 ascending interoceptive signaling regulates osteoblastic energy homeostasis to induce bone formation.
source: Taken together, our results indicate that NPY downregulated by PGE2/EP4 ascending interoceptive signaling regulates osteoblastic energy homeostasis to induce bone formation.
evidence: The claim is an interpretation of the experimental data showing that SW033291 induces bone formation accompanied by FA uptake in osteoblasts in an EP4-dependent manner.

claim: Expression of Lipe and Pnpla2 increased significantly with injection of SW033291 compared with vehicle mice, and the lipolysis activity was abrogated in the AvilCre:Ptger4fl/fl mice.
source: Expression of Lipe (hormone sensitive lipase, hsl), which hydrolyses intracellular triglycerides into free FAs, and Pnpla2 (adipose triglyceride lipase, atgl), increased significantly with injection of SW033291 compared with that of vehicle mice, and the lipolysis activity was abrogated in the AvilCre:Ptger4fl/fl mice (Figure 5A and B).
evidence: The claim is supported by RT-PCR data shown in Figures 5A and 5B.

claim: FA concentration in circulation was higher in AvilCre:Ptger4fl/fl mice compared with their WT littermates.
source: FA concentration in circulation was higher in AvilCre:Ptger4fl/fl mice compared with their WT littermates (Figure 5C).
evidence: The claim is supported by serum FA measurements shown in Figure 5C.

claim: FA concentration decreased significantly with injection of SW033291 in WT mice but not in AvilCre:Ptger4fl/fl mice.
source: FA concentration decreased significantly with injection of SW033291 in WT mice but not in AvilCre:Ptger4fl/fl mice (Figure 5C)
evidence: The claim is supported by serum FA measurements shown in Figure 5C.

claim: pAMPK expression was significantly increased in the perilipin+ adipocytes in WT mice, but the catabolic effect of SW033291 on adipocytes was impaired in AvilCre:Ptger4fl/fl mice.
source: Immunostaining of white adipose tissue sections showed that pAMPK expression was significantly increased in the perilipin+ adipocytes in WT mice, but the catabolic effect of SW033291 on adipocytes was impaired in AvilCre:Ptger4fl/fl mice (Figure 5D and E).
evidence: The claim is supported by immunofluorescence staining data shown in Figures 5D and 5E.

claim: Bone marrow fat decreased significantly with injection of SW033291 in WT mice, but this effect was abrogated in AvilCre:Ptger4fl/fl mice.
source: To validate deposition of FAs in adipose tissue in the bone marrow, we performed osmium tetroxide (OsO4) staining of fat droplets in decalcified femurs captured by µCT, which showed that bone marrow fat decreased significantly with injection of SW033291 in WT mice, but this effect was abrogated in AvilCre:Ptger4fl/fl mice (Figure 5F and G).
evidence: The claim is supported by OsO4 staining and μCT data shown in Figures 5F and 5G.

claim: Stimulation of skeletal interoception induces adipose catabolic activity in bone marrow and white adipose tissue by downregulating NPY expression in the hypothalamus.
source: Collectively, these data indicate that stimulation of skeletal interoception induces adipose catabolic activity in bone marrow and white adipose tissue by downregulating NPY expression in the hypothalamus.
evidence: The claim is an interpretation of the experimental data showing that SW033291 induces lipolysis markers and reduces fat mass in an EP4-dependent manner.

claim: NPY expression significantly increased in serum and ARC in BglapCre:Cox2fl/fl relative to the WT group.
source: We found NPY expression significantly increased in serum and ARC in BglapCre:Cox2fl/fl relative to the WT group (Figure 5H and I).
evidence: The claim is supported by ELISA and immunofluorescence data shown in Figures 5H and 5I.

claim: BglapCre:Cox2fl/fl mice show decrease of osteoblastic differentiation along with adipocytes accumulation.
source: Immunofluorescence also demonstrated decrease of osteoblastic differentiation along with adipocytes accumulation in BglapCre:Cox2fl/fl as evidenced by decrease of osteocalcin positive osteoblasts and increase of perilipin positive adipocytes (Figure 5J).
evidence: The claim is supported by immunofluorescence staining data shown in Figure 5J.

claim: Expression of FA oxidation related gene Cpt1b and Fatp1 in osteoblasts significantly decreased in BglapCre:Cox2fl/fl relative to WT group.
source: Moreover, expression of FA oxidation related gene Cpt1b and Fatp1 in osteoblasts significantly decreased in BglapCre:Cox2fl/fl relative to WT group (Figure 5K).
evidence: The claim is supported by RT-PCR data shown in Figure 5K.

claim: Osteoblasts derived PGE2 regulate hypothalamic NPY expression via skeleton sensory interoceptive signals maintain osteoblastic energy homeostasis and FA oxidation.
source: Taken together, these results showed that osteoblasts derived PGE2 regulate hypothalamic NPY expression via skeleton sensory interoceptive signals maintain osteoblastic energy homeostasis and FA oxidation.
evidence: The claim is an interpretation of the experimental data from BglapCre:Cox2fl/fl mice showing that osteoblast-specific COX2 deletion increases NPY and decreases FA oxidation.

claim: The bone loss phenotype in AvilCre:Ptger4fl/fl mice was rescued by BIBO3304.
source: Interestingly, the bone loss phenotype in AvilCre:Ptger4fl/fl mice was rescued by BIBO3304, as shown by µCT (Figure 6A and B)
evidence: The claim is supported by μCT data shown in Figures 6A and 6B.

claim: Elevation of PGE2 by injection of SW033291 did not rescue the bone loss in AvilCre:Ptger4fl/fl mice.
source: whereas elevation of PGE2 by injection of SW033291 did not rescue the bone loss in AvilCre:Ptger4fl/fl mice (Figure 4A through 4D).
evidence: The claim is supported by data shown in Figures 4A through 4D showing no rescue of bone loss in AvilCre:Ptger4fl/fl mice with SW033291.

claim: The number of osteocalcin+ osteoblasts did not change with BIBO3304 in AvilCre:Ptger4fl/fl mice.
source: Immunohistologic analysis showed that the number of osteocalcin+ osteoblasts did not change with BIBO3304 in AvilCre:Ptger4fl/fl mice (Figure 6C and D)
evidence: The claim is supported by immunohistochemistry data shown in Figures 6C and 6D.

claim: Injection of BIBO3304 significantly increased levels of pCREB in osteocalcin+ osteoblasts at the bone surface in AvilCre:Ptger4fl/fl mice.
source: Injection of BIBO3304 significantly increased levels of pCREB in osteocalcin+ osteoblasts at the bone surface in AvilCre:Ptger4fl/fl mice (Figure 6E)
evidence: The claim is supported by immunofluorescence staining data shown in Figure 6E.

claim: cAMP concentration was increased in osteoblasts of AvilCre:Ptger4fl/fl mice injected with BIBO3304.
source: and cAMP concentration was also increased (Figure 6F).
evidence: The claim is supported by cAMP concentration measurements shown in Figure 6F.

claim: AvilCre:Ptger4fl/fl mice injected with BIBO3304 had significantly increased expression of osteogenesis markers Runx2, Alp, and Col1a1.
source: Importantly, AvilCre:Ptger4fl/fl mice injected with BIBO3304 had significantly increased expression of osteogenesis markers Runx2, Alp, and Col1a1 (Figure 6G).
evidence: The claim is supported by RT-PCR data shown in Figure 6G.

claim: The expression of FA oxidation factors Fatp1 and Cpt1b in osteoblasts decreased in AvilCre:Ptger4fl/fl mice but was rescued with injection of BIBO3304.
source: The expression of FA oxidation factors Fatp1 and Cpt1b in osteoblasts decreased in AvilCre:Ptger4fl/fl mice but was rescued with injection of BIBO3304 (Figure 6H).
evidence: The claim is supported by RT-PCR data shown in Figure 6H.

claim: The levels of FAs were significantly increased in AvilCre:Ptger4fl/fl mice and significantly decreased with injection of BIBO3304.
source: Moreover, the levels of FAs were significantly increased in AvilCre:Ptger4fl/fl mice and significantly decreased with injection of BIBO3304 (Figure 6I)
evidence: The claim is supported by serum FA measurements shown in Figure 6I.

claim: BIBO3304 significantly increased lipolysis marker Lipe and Pnpla2 expression in AvilCre:Ptger4fl/fl mice.
source: In addition, BIBO3304 significantly increased lipolysis marker Lipe and Pnpla2 expression in AvilCre:Ptger4fl/fl mice (Figure 6J)
evidence: The claim is supported by RT-PCR data shown in Figure 6J.

claim: BIBO3304 augmented catabolic metabolism of adipocytes in AvilCre:Ptger4fl/fl mice as shown with an increase of pAMPK.
source: and augmented catabolic metabolism of adipocytes in AvilCre:Ptger4fl/fl mice as shown with an increase of pAMPK (Figure 6K).
evidence: The claim is supported by immunofluorescence staining data shown in Figure 6K.

claim: Accumulated marrow fat droplets in AvilCre:Ptger4fl/fl mice were significantly lower with injection of BIBO3304 relative to that of AvilCre:Ptger4fl/fl mice with vehicle injection.
source: Accordingly, accumulated marrow fat droplets in AvilCre:Ptger4fl/fl mice were significantly lower with injection of BIBO3304 relative to that of AvilCre:Ptger4fl/fl mice with vehicle injection (Figure 6L and M).
evidence: The claim is supported by OsO4 staining and μCT data shown in Figures 6L and 6M.

claim: Ascending PGE2/EP4 skeleton interoceptive signaling induces commitment of MSCs to osteoblast lineages, whereas downregulation of NPY expression in the hypothalamus promotes osteoblast differentiation by increasing FA oxidation in osteoblasts and lipolysis in adipocytes as a parallel descending neuroendocrine interoceptive pathway.
source: Taken together, our data indicate that ascending PGE2/EP4 skeleton interoceptive signaling induces commitment of MSCs to osteoblast lineages, whereas downregulation of NPY expression in the hypothalamus promotes osteoblast differentiation by increasing FA oxidation in osteoblasts and lipolysis in adipocytes as a parallel descending neuroendocrine interoceptive pathway.
evidence: The claim is an interpretation of the experimental data showing distinct mechanisms for PGE2/EP4 interoception (MSC commitment) and NPY downregulation (osteoblast differentiation).

claim: YFP+ osterix+ preosteoblasts and YFP+ osteocalcin+ osteoblasts increased significantly with injection of β2R antagonist propranolol.
source: Fate mapping assay showed that YFP+ osterix+ preosteoblasts and YFP+ osteocalcin+ osteoblasts increased significantly with injection of β2R antagonist, propranolol (Prop).
evidence: The claim is supported by fate mapping data from LeprCre:Rosa26lsl-EYFP mice.

claim: Injection of high affinity Y1R agonist [Leu31, Pro34]-NPY did not change the number of YFP+ osterix+ preosteoblasts relative to vehicle treatment, but YFP+ osteocalcin+ osteoblasts decreased significantly.
source: Interestingly, injection of high affinity Y1R agonist [Leu31, Pro34]-NPY did not change the number of YFP+ osterix+ preosteoblasts relative to vehicle treatment, but YFP+ osteocalcin+ osteoblasts decreased significantly
evidence: The claim is supported by fate mapping data from LeprCre:Rosa26lsl-EYFP mice.

claim: Co-injection of propranolol and [Leu31,Pro34]-NPY significantly increased YFP+osterix+ preosteoblasts and still significantly decreased YFP+ osteoblasts relative to control groups.
source: Furthermore, co-injection of propranolol and [Leu31,Pro34]-NPY significantly increased YFP+osterix+ preosteoblasts and still significantly decreased YFP+ osteoblasts relative to control groups (Figure 7A through 7C)
evidence: The claim is supported by fate mapping data shown in Figures 7A through 7C.

claim: CFU-F and CFU-Ob assay showed significant increase with propranolol treatment relative to vehicle.
source: CFU-F and CFU-Ob assay showed significant increase with propranolol treatment relative to vehicle.
evidence: The claim is supported by CFU assay data.

claim: [Leu31, Pro34]-NPY treatment significantly reduced CFU-Ob with no significant changes in CFU-F.
source: [Leu31, Pro34]-NPY treatment significantly reduced CFU-Ob with no significant changes in CFU-F.
evidence: The claim is supported by CFU assay data.

claim: The combination of propranolol and [Leu31, Pro34]-NPY significantly increased CFU-F but decreased CFU-Ob.
source: As expected, the combination of propranolol and [Leu31, Pro34]-NPY significantly increased CFU-F but decreased CFU-Ob (Figure 7D through 7F).
evidence: The claim is supported by CFU assay data shown in Figures 7D through 7F.

claim: PGE2/EP4 ascending interoceptive signaling downregulates sympathetic activity and β2R signaling for the commitment of MSCs.
source: Therefore, our data show that PGE2/EP4 ascending interoceptive signaling downregulates sympathetic activity and β2R signaling for the of MSCs.
evidence: The claim is an interpretation of the fate mapping and CFU assay data showing that β2R antagonist increases MSC commitment to osteoblasts.

claim: PGE2/EP4 ascending interoceptive signaling downregulates expression of NPY in hypothalamus to regulate fat and bone metabolism in facilitation of osteoblast differentiation.
source: In parallel, PGE2/EP4 ascending interoceptive signaling downregulates expression of NPY in hypothalamus to regulate fat and bone metabolism in facilitation of osteoblast differentiation (Figure 7G).
evidence: The claim is an interpretation of the experimental data showing that PGE2/EP4 signaling regulates NPY expression and affects both bone and fat metabolism.

claim: The central nervous system regulates activity of peripheral organs through interoception.
source: The central nervous system regulates activity of peripheral organs through interoception.
evidence: The claim is stated in the abstract as background knowledge.

claim: PGE2/EP4 skeleton interception regulate bone homeostasis.
source: In our previous study, we have demonstrated that PGE2/EP4 skeleton interception regulate bone homeostasis.
evidence: The claim references previous work by the authors.

claim: Ascending skeleton interoceptive signaling downregulates expression of hypothalamic neuropeptide Y (NPY) and induce lipolysis of adipose tissue for osteoblastic bone formation.
source: Here, we show that ascending skeleton interoceptive signaling downregulates expression of hypothalamic neuropeptide Y (NPY) and induce lipolysis of adipose tissue for osteoblastic bone formation.
evidence: The claim is the main finding stated in the abstract, supported by the experimental data throughout the manuscript.

claim: The ascending skeleton interoceptive signaling induces expression of small heterodimer partner-interacting leucine zipper protein (SMILE) in the hypothalamus.
source: Specifically, the ascending skeleton interoceptive signaling induces expression of small heterodimer partner-interacting leucine zipper protein (SMILE) in the hypothalamus.
evidence: The claim is stated in the abstract and supported by Western blot and immunostaining data in Figure 3.

claim: SMILE binds to pCREB as a transcriptional heterodimer on Npy promoters to inhibit NPY expression.
source: SMILE binds to pCREB as a transcriptional heterodimer on Npy promoters to inhibit NPY expression.
evidence: The claim is stated in the abstract and supported by ChIP assay data in Figure 3.

claim: Knockout of EP4 in sensory nerve increases expression of NPY causing bone catabolism and fat anabolism.
source: Knockout of EP4 in sensory nerve increases expression of NPY causing bone catabolism and fat anabolism.
evidence: The claim is stated in the abstract and supported by data from AvilCre:Ptger4fl/fl mice showing increased NPY, decreased bone mass, and increased fat mass.

claim: Inhibition of NPY Y1 receptor (Y1R) accelerated oxidation of free fatty acids in osteoblasts and rescued bone loss in AvilCre:Ptger4fl/fl mice.
source: Importantly, inhibition of NPY Y1 receptor (Y1R) accelerated oxidation of free fatty acids in osteoblasts and rescued bone loss in AvilCre:Ptger4fl/fl mice.
evidence: The claim is stated in the abstract and supported by data from BIBO3304 treatment experiments in Figure 6.

claim: Downregulation of hypothalamic NPY expression lipolyzes free fatty acids for anabolic bone formation through a neuroendocrine descending interoceptive regulation.
source: Thus, downregulation of hypothalamic NPY expression lipolyzes free fatty acids for anabolic bone formation through a neuroendocrine descending interoceptive regulation.
evidence: The claim is the main conclusion stated in the abstract, supported by the experimental data throughout the manuscript.

claim: CNS receives interoceptive signals originating from peripheral tissues by ascending pathways for interpretation and integration to regulate the activity of specific organs through descending pathways.
source: CNS receives interoceptive signals originating from peripheral tissues by ascending pathways for interpretation and integration to regulate the activity of specific organs through descending pathways (Chen et al., 2021).
evidence: The claim is stated as background knowledge with citation to Chen et al., 2021.

claim: The skeleton is the largest organ in the body and stores vital minerals, forms muscle attachments and comprises the niches for hematopoiesis.
source: The skeleton is the largest organ in the body and stores vital minerals, forms muscle attachments and comprises the niches for hematopoiesis (Leider, 1947).
evidence: The claim is stated as background knowledge with citation to Leider, 1947.

claim: The skeleton is innervated abundantly by sensory nerves, not only to sense pain, but to contribute to bone anabolism.
source: The skeleton is innervated abundantly by sensory nerves, not only to sense pain, but to contribute to bone anabolism (Brazill et al., 2019; Fukuda et al., 2013).
evidence: The claim is stated as background knowledge with citations to Brazill et al., 2019 and Fukuda et al., 2013.

claim: The loss of sensory nerves in bone impairs bone mass formation.
source: The loss of sensory nerves in bone impairs bone mass formation (Fukuda et al., 2013).
evidence: The claim is stated as background knowledge with citation to Fukuda et al., 2013.
